title: Inquest into man's shooting begins
article: An inquest into the shooting death of a mentally ill man begins today in Brockville.

Dr. Roger Skinner will lead the inquest into the death of Matthew Roke, who was a 33-year-old man suffering from schizophrenia when he was fatally shot during a roadside encounter with provincial police officers in May 2012.
The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding Roke's death and the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.

Roke was shot in the early morning hours of May 2, 2012. Members of the Ontario Provincial Police Grenville County detachment were involved in an altercation with Roke near the carpool lot by the Highway 401 ramps in Maitland. Roke is alleged to have lunged at police officers while holding a knife before he was fatally shot.

The province's Special Investigations Unit, which looks into incidents involving police that result in death or serious injury, investigated the Roke incident and afterwards cleared the two police officers involved in the shooting. The SIU found "Roke made it clear he did not intend to comply" with orders from officers to put down his weapon.
The SIU report also stated one officer feared for his life while the other feared for the safety of his partner.

Five shots were fired during the confrontation; of those, one hit Roke in the left thigh, a second in the right leg and two struck him in the right side of his chest, causing his death, the SIU concluded.
When reached Monday, Roke's mother Jody said the family was not prepared to speak before the inquest.
However, she told QMI Agency in March the family was hoping for something positive to come out of the inquest.
"We're just trying to bring something good out of this and get people to pay more attention," Jody Roke said at the time.
"We will speak about how it all went with Matt and how it could go differently."
She also said at the time she hopes the inquest will address issues between the police and people suffering from mental illness.
Sixteen witnesses, including Jody and her husband John, are expected to speak during the inquest, which will be held at St. Lawrence College.
